name: Computer Science, Ph.D.

deadline.value: Fall I priority deadline is April 30, 2027 (final deadline July 15, 2027) for both domestic and international applicants; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority filing strongly recommended for funding and advisor alignment.
deadline.quote: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; however, applying by the priority deadline is strongly recommended—especially for applicants seeking faculty alignment and funding consideration. | Priority Deadline | April 30 | Final Deadline | July 15

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not required at this time for admission to the Ph.D. in Computer Science.
gre_general.quote: GRE scores are not required at this time.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists in Computer Science; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must identify a potential faculty advisor before applying, and admission is contingent on faculty support and research alignment.
supervisor.quote: Applicants will be asked to indicate a potential faculty advisor as part of the application. | Admission is contingent on faculty support and research alignment.

also.quote: Persons seeking admission to the COSC program should first contact the program to identify a faculty member willing to serve as their graduate advisor. Applicants will not be admitted to the program without a graduate faculty advisor.

funding.value: Limited teaching and research assistantships (at least 10 graduate assistantships awarded yearly across the program), faculty-led research funding, and competitive NSF CREST-GEIMS Doctoral Fellowships ($1,800-$2,400/month plus tuition and fees for Geospatial Informatics fellows) are available; 50% FTE assistantships qualify international students for in-state tuition under Texas Education Code 54.212.
funding.quote: A limited number of research and teaching assistantships are available each year. Many students are supported through faculty-led research projects, depending on funding availability and research alignment.

also.quote: Each year, the Geospatial Computer Science, PhD Program awards at least 10 graduate assistantships to students.

The NSF CREST-GEIMS Center at TAMU-CC offers a competitive Fellowship to Ph.D. students pursuing doctoral degrees in Coastal and Marine Systems Science (CMSS) or Computer Science with a Geospatial focus at TAMU-CC.

According to the Texas Education Code, Section 54.212, non-resident students receiving a 50% FTE graduate assistantship will receive in-state tuition and fees at the rate charged to Texas residents for the semester in which they hold the assistantship appointment.

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter with either a bachelor's degree (75 semester credit hours minimum) or a master's degree (57 semester credit hours minimum) in computer science or a closely related field.
entry_route.quote: Applicants may enter the program with either a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science or a closely related field.

notes: Offers an optional specialization in Geospatial Informatics (previously titled Geospatial Computer Science on earlier catalog/research pages); no standalone Data Science Ph.D. track exists. Ph.D. Geospatial Computer Science applicants are exempt from third-party foreign transcript evaluation and may submit official academic credentials/transcripts directly.
